descriptionChirho: The thumb of the hand or the big toe of the foot, a body part featured prominently in priestly consecration and leper purification rituals (Leviticus, Exodus). Singular construct and plural construct forms both denote the same anatomical referent. Multilingual evidence confirms a single sense: eng 'thumb/big-toe', spa 'pulgar/dedo-gordo', hin 'अंगूठे', arb 'إِبْهَام/أَباهِم', kor '엄지/엄지발가락', swa 'kidole kikubwa/vidole vikubwa'.
